item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Major Housing & Development Reforms:** Council will consider significant changes to city zoning rules, including allowing more diverse housing types ("missing middle housing"), reducing minimum parking requirements, and easing regulations for home-based businesses. * **City Boundary Adjustments:** Multiple public hearings are scheduled to disannex properties from Austin's jurisdiction, a process mandated by new state legislation (SB 1844). * **Key City Plans:** Votes are expected on Austin's 2025-2027 Strategic Plan to address homelessness and a public hearing will be held on adopting the Austin Core Transportation Plan for future mobility. * **Parkland and Signage Debates:** Public hearings will address allowing the permanent use of a portion of Auditorium Shores parkland for a water line and proposed changes to city billboard and sign regulations.

item.title: Austin Austin Housing Finance Corporation: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation agenda: * **Affordable Housing Loan:** The Austin Housing Finance Corporation (AHFC) will consider approving a $3.5 million loan to National Church Residences for the development of Sunday Village, an affordable housing project located near 1026 Clayton Lane. * **Funding Source:** If approved, this $3.5 million will be drawn from the AHFC's Fiscal Year 2025-26 Capital Budget to support local housing initiatives. * **No Public Hearings:** The agenda for this meeting does not include any specific public hearings.

item.title: Austin Work Session: March 24, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Major Housing Policy Changes:** Council will discuss initiating significant amendments to zoning laws to allow for more diverse housing options, including "missing middle housing" like townhomes and cottage courts, and "mixed-use" developments combining residential and commercial spaces. * **Strategic Plan to Address Homelessness:** A new 2025-2027 Strategic Plan for addressing homelessness in Austin will be presented for review. * **Public Hearing on Sign Regulations:** A public hearing will be held on a proposal to amend city code to potentially allow larger, electronic, and off-premises advertising signs in public areas. * **I-35 Cap and Stitch Project Update:** Council members will receive a briefing on the latest recommendations for the I-35 Cap and Stitch project.

item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 12, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Massive Infrastructure Investment:** Council will consider significant funding, including increasing an EPA loan to $1 billion and approving a $600 million contract amendment, for the expansion of the Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant, bringing the project's total cost to $1.5 billion. * **Major Land Use Decisions & Zoning Changes:** A key item involves initiating the rezoning of the 445-acre Jimmy Clay and Roy Kizer Golf Courses. The agenda also includes multiple public hearings on zoning and land use amendments across the city, proposing changes that could increase density or alter property uses, including a contentious request to allow liquor sales on East Cesar Chavez Street. * **Updates to Lobbyist Transparency Rules:** Council will review an ordinance to amend the City Code, revising definitions and reporting requirements for lobbyists to enhance transparency in communications with City officials. * **Affordable Housing & Local Business Support:** Items include advancing a mixed-use development at 800 E. St. John Avenue with goals for deeper affordability, and an economic development agreement to support The Vortex, a local cultural business.

item.title: Austin Austin Housing Finance Corporation: March 12, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation agenda: * The **Austin Housing Finance Corporation (AHFC)** is meeting to discuss a key housing initiative. * The main item on the agenda is a proposal to authorize a **$5.5 million loan** for "The Bloom at Lamar Square," a new multifamily rental development planned for 1326 and 1328 Lamar Square Drive. This funding aims to increase housing options in Austin. * This meeting, scheduled for March 12, 2026, at 10:30 AM at Austin City Hall, **does not include any public hearings**.
